summary: In this excerpt from Book 6 (part 77) of a fiction serial, the narrator is captured by a group of armed men and taken in a van. Handcuffed and searched, he is brought before a sinister figure called the Lancer, who sits in the back of the van fidgeting with meditation balls and speaking in a foreign language to his men. The narrator admits he helped Halliday with her proof, claims the NSA tried to recruit him, and tries to appear a helpless street mathematician while the Lancer offers him a deal: help them or be killed.
one_line: A captured narrator is questioned by a menacing figure called the Lancer in a van, after admitting he helped Halliday with her proof.
key_facts: The narrator was searched, and the men took the gun he had stolen from a DHS agent, along with his burner cell phone and other pocket contents.
The narrator was handcuffed to the door of a van and followed the men into another van, which was one of a fleet of vans and SUVs.
A middle-aged man sat in the back of the van out of sight of the security cameras, described as having bronze skin, greasy brown hair around a bald spot, and a long, lantern-jawed face.
The Lancer held a set of meditation balls in one hand that made a clack, clack, clack sound as they turned.
The Lancer had an intricately carved walking stick by his knee and a tablet computer balanced on his lap.
The narrator told the Lancer that a lot of people were after him, and said that he had helped Halliday with her proof.
The narrator said of helping Halliday with her proof: "In case you're wondering, it wasn't worth it."
The narrator asked, "Are you the Lancer?" and the meditation balls stopped as the Lancer's piercing gaze fixed on him.
The narrator invented a story that the NSA had tried to grab him because they thought he was working for the Lancer.
The Lancer said, "I have many names," and sneered at the United States National Security Agency, calling its games stupid.
The narrator said the NSA had tried to offer him a deal, and that they weren't offering enough, which he admitted was reckless.
The Lancer offered the narrator a deal: "you help us, we won't kill you."
